gates.text: Truth: no claim, number, customer, quote or result that isn't in confirmed facts or cited research; gaps are marked [NEEDS FACT: …].
No fabricated customer evidence: no personas, quotes, review counts or demographics that cannot be traced to a source.
Swap test: the core positioning line and headline options do not work unchanged for the top named competitor.
No superlative fog: no unsourced 'best', '#1', 'leading', 'world-class', 'seamless' or 'cutting-edge'.

anchors.1: Only lists named competitors, or none.
anchors.3: Lists competitors and one generic substitute.
anchors.5: Names the real status-quo alternatives, including a non-product one, with evidence of switching ('switched from…') and counts.

anchors.1: Parity claims (quality, service, affordable); fails the swap test.
anchors.5: Unique attributes tied to value through a so-what chain, each evidenced; parity attributes removed; passes the swap test.

anchors.3: Outcomes named but not quantified or grounded in customer words.
anchors.5: Concrete outcomes in customer language, quantified where data exists, clustered into 1–3 themes.
Segment by observable traits plus a trigger event plus disqualifiers.
Frame chosen from 2–3 candidates tested for obviousness of value and price expectation; style (big fish small pond / head-to-head / new category) justified with rejected options.

anchors.3: Some quotes, mostly from the business's own site.
anchors.5: Verbatim VoC across 3+ sources with counts and links behind each value theme.
3 headline and 3 subhead options on different angles, pillars with proof, objection lines, words to use/avoid, and a pitch narrative in section or slide order.
High/Medium/Low confidence per component with the reason; a 2–3 week validation plan with metric, minimum volume, decision rule and dates.
